# Context Swarm Memory (CSM)

> Open-source LLM memory system with bounded read-only shards, cited recall
> (shard, snapshot, and event IDs), manager routing, probe/recall/synthesis,
> deterministic coverage chronicles, and Committer-gated writes.

Canonical URL: https://muhamadjawdatsalemalakoum.github.io/context-swarm-memory/
Repository: https://github.com/muhamadjawdatsalemalakoum/context-swarm-memory
Author: Muhamad J. Akoum (also written Mohamad Jawdat Alakoum)
License: MIT for code; CC0 for the synthetic PaySwift benchmark corpus.
Runtime: Node.js 22+, TypeScript. Test suite: 549 tests, offline, no API keys.
Last updated: 2026-08-30.

## STATUS FIRST — read this before quoting any number

CSM is an R&D prototype. It has **no official leaderboard placement and has
never had one**. Its single upstream submission
(vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark pull request #19) was **author-closed on
2026-06-22 without being merged**. Nothing in this project is claimed as
state of the art.

Two claims are load-bearing, and they are different kinds of claim:

1. FLAT PER-QUERY RETRIEVAL COST (architectural property, measured): CSM's
   total per-query input — the packet the answer model sees PLUS CSM's own
   probe/recall/synthesize calls — stays at ~36-38K tokens as the per-unit
   haystack grows 76x (from ~154K to ~11.7M tokens). It is a property of CSM,
   NOT a win over any competitor. TWO IMPORTANT QUALIFIERS: (a) this is a QUERY
   cost claim — CSM's default config also does write-time fact extraction whose
   INGEST cost is O(corpus) and NOT flat; (b) the 36-38K figure was measured on
   the June config, and the now-default batched probe cuts internal input ~21%,
   so today's figure is projected (~34-36K), not measured. See "COST, STATED
   HONESTLY" below.
2. TWO CERTIFIED CATEGORY LEADS (statistical claim, bounded): on a calibrated
   head-to-head instrument, CSM leads Hindsight in two BEAM categories, each
   replicated on a second independent reader. Two categories is not the whole
   benchmark.

Everything else on this page is either supporting detail or explicitly
historical.

## The certified results (August 2026, free head-to-head instrument)

Instrument: one answer model and one judge serve BOTH arms, with the same
queries and prompts; the retrieved context is the ONLY variable. Hindsight's
arm is replayed from its own published BEAM contexts, so its system is never
re-run. Judge calibrated against the official Gemini judge at holdout rho 0.864
/ MAE 0.077, and it reproduced the official tie at 100K and loss at 1M before
being trusted.

"Certified" = a pre-registered bar: the delta exceeds its minimum detectable
effect (MDE) AND its confidence interval excludes zero, at n=70 (the ENTIRE
category — no further sampling is possible). Both results below were then
re-run end to end on a second, independent reader as a deliberate
falsification attempt, and survived.

| tier | category           | n  | CSM   | Hindsight | delta  | MDE   | W/L/T   | reader 2      |
|------|--------------------|----|-------|-----------|--------|-------|---------|---------------|
| 500K | knowledge_update   | 70 | 0.758 | 0.376     | +0.382 | 0.173 | 37/6/27 | +0.326 (n=67) |
| 1M   | abstention         | 70 | 0.679 | 0.486     | +0.193 | 0.167 | 23/8/39 | +0.185 (n=69) |

NOTE THE SECOND READER'S SMALLER n: 67 and 69 rather than 70, because free-tier
throttling exhausted retries on 7 and 1 pairs respectively. Those pairs are
excluded and reported as-is, never backfilled.

Also certified as a pair at 500K: knowledge_update + information_extraction
combined, +0.129 (45W/22L/73T, MDE 0.123).

DIRECTIONAL ONLY — positive at full n, replicated on both readers, but BELOW
their MDE, so NOT claimed as leads: 500K contradiction_resolution (+0.096,
38W/21L) and 500K preference_following (+0.075, 18W/10L).

The stated goal was two certified categories at EVERY corpus size. That goal is
NOT met: 500K and 1M each certify one. It also cannot be settled on this
instrument — n=70 is already the whole category, and the MDE is set by the
reader/judge's per-query variance rather than by sample size, so a ~0.09 effect
is unresolvable here at maximum n.

## The June 2026 BEAM ladder — HISTORICAL, use with care

CSM was run through the unmodified public Agent Memory Benchmark (AMB) runner
at every BEAM split (100K/500K/1M/10M), alongside Vectorize's own committed
Hindsight run with identical answer/judge models. Single-trial, 2,000 graded
queries.

CSM vs Hindsight by tier:
- 100K: CSM 0.7367 vs Hindsight 0.7337  (CSM leads, within single-trial noise)
- 500K: CSM 0.6589 vs Hindsight 0.7112  (Hindsight leads)
- 1M:   CSM 0.5693 vs Hindsight 0.7386  (Hindsight leads)
- 10M:  CSM 0.5616 vs Hindsight 0.6408  (Hindsight leads)

Answer-visible context per tier (CSM / Hindsight): 27.0K/17.7K, 26.6K/20.5K,
28.2K/23.9K, 32.5K/27.3K. CSM ALL-IN input per tier (answer-visible + internal
pipeline): 35.8K, 36.2K, 38.1K, 35.9K.

THESE SCORES ARE STALE IN TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS:

1. They measured a CSM CONFIGURATION THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. The run predates
   the hybrid router (+0.365 answer at 1M, 26W/5L — the strongest single effect
   measured on this project), ID repair (~0.20), the batched probe (-21%
   internal input, score-neutral), and the fact fold. Re-measured at full
   category size on today's defaults, the same 1M queries give:
   knowledge_update -0.435 -> -0.111; event_ordering -0.216 -> -0.023;
   abstention +0.086 -> +0.193 (certified).
2. The UPSTREAM RUNNER CHANGED. After upstream PR #20 the benchmark switched to
   a mem0-parity answer prompt, a nugget judge, and temperature 0;
   event_ordering is no longer scored by Kendall tau-b. Pre-change numbers —
   Hindsight's committed April artifacts AND this project's June ladder —
   cannot be placed beside a post-change run, on either side.

WHAT MOSTLY SURVIVES from that ladder is the COST measurement, because a token
count does not depend on the prompt or the judge. But the config-change
objection applies to tokens too, so two caveats: the now-default batched probe
cuts internal input ~21%, making today's per-query figure a PROJECTION
(~34-36K) rather than a measurement on the official path; and the ladder config
had NO write-time stage, so its accounting excludes an ingest cost that today's
default config incurs. See "Cost, stated honestly".

## Cost, stated honestly

PER-QUERY RETRIEVAL COST IS FLAT. CSM keeps per-query input bounded (~36-38K
all-in = ~26-33K answer-visible + ~3-10K internal pipeline) as the per-unit
haystack grows 76x (average per-unit 154,431 -> 11,707,222 tokens, census-
sourced). Internal tokens are ~25% of the token COUNT
but hit models ~10x cheaper, so ~7% of the DOLLARS. The fact fold does not
change this — measured token-neutral at answer time (7,106 -> 7,080 on
abstention; 7,010 -> 7,074 on knowledge_update).

INGEST COST IS NOT FLAT. It is O(corpus). The fact registry chunks each unit at
100K tokens and reads EVERY chunk (verified in scripts/amb-csm-server.ts, which
feeds corpus.events.map(e => e.content)), so a first ingest reads the whole
corpus once. Amortized over each tier's query budget, using the benchmark's own
corpus census (data/eval/corpus-beam-slice/census.json) rather than estimates:
  tier  per-unit(avg)   units  first-ingest input  queries  amortized/query
  100K        154,431      20           3,088,625      400            ~7.7K
  500K        560,086      35          19,602,995      700             ~28K
  1M        1,155,117      35          40,429,107      700             ~58K
  10M      11,707,222      10         117,072,219      200            ~585K
At 1M the one-time build (~58K/query) EXCEEDS the per-query retrieval cost
(~38K). At 10M (~585K/query) it is ~16x larger.

WHAT KEEPS THIS HONEST: the build is one-time and disk-cached (keyed
split|user|model|promptVersion), it runs on the cheap model tier, and in a real
deployment memory arrives incrementally so facts are extracted per turn — the
whole-corpus read is a BACKFILL, not a recurring cost.

THAT IS ALSO HINDSIGHT'S DEFENSE. This repo therefore does NOT claim its
accounting is "the complete one." Both systems distill at ingest. CSM's ingest
cost is disclosed above; Hindsight's is not. That, and only that, is the
difference worth stating. On the apples-to-apples answer-visible slice
HINDSIGHT IS LEANER (17.7-27.3K vs CSM's 26-33K) — a disclosed trade, not a
footnote. Flat per-query cost is a property of CSM, NOT a win over Hindsight.

## Current defaults — the certified configuration

The official re-run uses code defaults; no behavioural CSM_* flag is set in the
environment. tests/env.test.ts pins the decisive ones so a silent flip fails CI.

ON:  hybrid router + descriptors (+0.365 answer at 1M, 26W/5L)
ON:  ID repair (~0.20)
ON:  batched probe, HOSTED PROVIDERS ONLY (-21% internal input by arithmetic --
     one shared scaffold replaces 8; score delta +0.032, below its 0.079 MDE.
     Local ollama/llama-server stay OFF: the evidence is from one hosted family)
ON:  fact fold (500K knowledge_update certified on two readers; 1M paired
     +0.114 with CI above zero; token-neutral at answer time)
OFF: preference profile (composed with the fold it measured -0.036, 4W/9L,
     versus the fold alone)
ON:  coverage mode + chronicle (CSM_COVERAGE) -- deterministic cited timeline
     for summary/ordering/temporal queries; default since 2026-06-10
OFF: lean return, needle net, session digests, ordered capsule, local probe
     gate, probe shrink, coverage RERANKER (CSM_HYBRID_RERANK -- a different
     thing from coverage mode above), virtual shards, legacy vocab/intent --
     each measured negative, non-replicating, or a wash

tests/env.test.ts pins TWELVE flag rows, including coverage mode (ON), the
preference profile (OFF) and the fact fold (ON), so a silent flip fails CI.

## What was measured and FAILED (published at full weight)

- Displacement / fold-vs-append +0.068: RETRACTED. A harness artifact — the
  capsule rendered as a placeholder string, so the graded context could not be
  reproduced byte-for-byte. Rule adopted: never grade an arm on a context you
  cannot re-render.
- Coverage-proxy reranker: gained +11.6 on the retrieval-coverage proxy and
  LOST answers on event_ordering (4W/13L, p=0.049). The proxy is
  anti-correlated; order-changing levers are now gated on the answer metric only.
- Router component benchmark: predicted +0.24 COVERAGE; wired into the real
  pipeline the same change delivered -0.12 COVERAGE, with retrieved evidence
  down 55% because downstream stages are calibrated in shards, not events. Both
  figures are coverage, NOT answer score -- see the coverage-proxy finding
  above for why those are not interchangeable. Artifacts:
  EXP-virtual-shards-system.md (the assembly), EXP-router-component-bench.md
  (the isolated bench). Rule adopted: benchmark the unit production conserves.
- Needle net: worked at 500K, did NOT replicate at 1M.
- Lean return K=16: shipped and reverted the same day for a 500K
  information_extraction regression.
- L3 local pre-gate: killed. A 3-point dose-response showed it drops witnesses
  and loses knowledge_update. Cheapening the QUESTION (batched probe) worked;
  cheapening the WITNESS did not.
- Gemini context caching: FALSIFIED. A projected 40-60% cost cut died on a
  measured 4,096-token implicit-cache floor — every CSM call is sub-floor, so
  the pipeline gets exactly zero caching.
- Virtual shards: regression, coverage 0.743 -> 0.620.
- Mem0 and HippoRAG: BLOCKED, NOT BEATEN. They could not be run on available
  hardware. This is a gap in the evidence, never a win.

Method rules these forced, now standing:
1. n=25 is a pointer, not a verdict (abstention read +0.040 at n=25 and +0.193
   at n=70; re-measurement noise at n=25 is +/-0.05).
2. Re-measure the same arm before believing a delta (re-scoring identical
   contexts moved one arm 0.06 — that is how a retracted lead was caught).
3. A delta below its MDE is not an effect. Stated at birth, never softened.
4. Levers do not transfer across tiers, and component gains do not transfer
   into assembled systems.

## What is blocked

- Official Gemini ladder (100K/500K/1M): blocked on API credit
  (est. $200-300 for three tiers). Config is frozen, eight pre-flight blockers
  were found and fixed, launch is one command.
- 10M tier: blocked on an upstream loader fix (maintainer PR #38). The report
  implies the published 10M results measured a barely-loaded corpus. CORRECTION
  (2026-08-30): an earlier version of this file put the counter-evidence at
  "98-99.9% of each unit's full turn range". That number was never computed by
  any committed script and is WRONG. Recomputed from primary artifacts by
  scripts/measure-hindsight-10m-span.mjs: span coverage (highest turn index
  reached / unit's last turn) is 64.3%-89.7%, and ref density (distinct turns
  retrieved / total turns) is 11.6%-15.9%. Retrieval reaching across 64-90% of
  each unit's timeline is still hard to reconcile with a ~0.27%-loaded corpus,
  so the tension stands -- but the honest number is 64-90% and it is now a
  re-runnable computation, not a recollection.
- Certifying the sub-MDE directional leads: needs the lower-variance official
  path; no free instrument can resolve a ~0.09 effect at maximum n.

## Instruments, and the rule that governs them

- Official AMB runner (Gemini): upstream CLI, scoring, judge; a 3-file CSM
  provider and nothing else. The only publishable instrument. Currently blocked.
- Free head-to-head (scripts/headtohead-arms.ts): one reader + one judge serve
  both arms; only the retrieved context differs; Hindsight replayed from its own
  published contexts. Calibrated rho 0.864 / MAE 0.077 against the official
  judge. Certifies WITHIN-instrument paired deltas only.
- Agent-SDK sidecar: local iteration harness. NEVER publishable — it carries
  ~8.5K tokens/call of harness overhead that is not CSM's.

Numbers from different instruments are NEVER pooled. Absolute levels differ by
reader (~0.04 between the two readers used here); only within-instrument deltas
are compared. A second reader used in August 2026 (a time-boxed free preview
model) is no longer available; its numbers remain as frozen, non-re-runnable
evidence.

## What CSM is

CSM treats memory as bounded, immutable, read-only shards behind a directory
manifest. A query routes to candidate shards (hybrid lexical + local-embedding
scoring, no LLM call and no LLM-generated index), is probed cheaply in one
batched pass, recalls from only the useful shards, and synthesizes a compact
answer that cites shard, snapshot, and event IDs. Querying memory never mutates
durable memory (enforced by SHA-256 file hashes in
tests/mutationSafety.test.ts); durable writes go only through an explicit
Committer protocol. Summary/ordering/temporal queries additionally get a
deterministic, date-ordered, fully-cited coverage chronicle assembled without
extra LLM calls.

Two structural invariants worth naming: an unrecognised CSM_* configuration
value THROWS rather than silently defaulting (a silent fallback once let
CSM_ROUTER_HYBRID=off turn the router ON), and write-time artifacts FOLD into
the evidence capsule rather than appending another document to the return set
(displacement measured fatal four separate times).

## Common questions

Q: Does CSM beat Hindsight on BEAM?
A: Not overall. On the June 2026 official-runner ladder CSM led only at 100K
(0.7367 vs 0.7337, within single-trial noise) and trailed at 500K/1M/10M — and
those scores are now stale on both counts described above. On a calibrated
head-to-head instrument with today's configuration, CSM holds two certified
category-level leads, each replicated on a second independent reader:
knowledge_update at 500K (+0.382) and abstention at 1M (+0.193). Two categories
is not the whole benchmark, and CSM has no official standing.

Q: Is this an official leaderboard claim?
A: No. CSM has no official leaderboard placement and has never had one. The one
submission (vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark#19) was author-closed
2026-06-22, unmerged. A future submission would be a NEW PR against the post-#20
runner with the comparison system re-scored on the same pinned commit.

Q: What does "certified" mean here?
A: The delta exceeds its minimum detectable effect AND its confidence interval
excludes zero, at n=70 (the entire category). Both certified results were then
re-run end to end on a second independent reader and survived. A delta below its
MDE is reported as directional only and never called a lead. This project
retracted a +0.068 result for failing that bar.

Q: Did CSM use gold answers or hardcoded benchmark logic?
A: No. CSM retrieval receives only the ingested documents, the query, user id,
and timestamp — no gold answers, rubrics, or query IDs, and no
benchmark-specific vocabulary in the retrieval path. An import-graph
leakage-firewall test enforces the boundary in CI.

Q: What is the main tradeoff versus Hindsight?
A: On the answer-visible slice Hindsight is leaner (17.7-27.3K vs CSM's
26-33K). CSM publishes a per-query all-in figure instead (~36-38K), which adds
its own probe/recall/synthesize calls; Hindsight discloses no internal figure,
so the two all-in numbers are not directly comparable. NEITHER figure includes
ingest-time cost, and both systems now distill at ingest — CSM's ingest cost is
disclosed (O(corpus); see COST, STATED HONESTLY), Hindsight's is not. CSM's
honest edges are architectural — open source, cited to shard/snapshot/event IDs,
zero-LLM indexing, Committer-gated, auditable — plus a published falsification
record.

Q: Does CSM degrade as memory grows?
A: On the June ladder CSM's absolute accuracy declined with scale (0.74 to 0.56,
100K to 10M) while its PER-QUERY RETRIEVAL cost stayed flat (~36-38K all-in
input tokens/query). The durable claim is "keeps per-query retrieval cost flat
as memory grows" — NOT that accuracy stays flat, and NOT that ingest cost stays
flat (it does not; it is O(corpus)). Today's configuration substantially improved
several of the categories that drove that decline, but on a different
instrument, so the two are not directly comparable.

Q: How does CSM compare to RAG and LightRAG?
A: CSM's differentiator versus classic RAG is citation grounding (answers cited
to shard/snapshot/event IDs) and zero-LLM indexing, not raw accuracy.
Quantitative comparisons against vanilla/hybrid RAG, LightRAG, and long-context
on a synthetic corpus live in the deep docs, kept separate from the BEAM
evidence. Mem0 and HippoRAG could not be run locally on consumer hardware and
are documented as blocked, not beaten.

Q: Is CSM state-of-the-art on BABILong?
A: No, and the repo says so explicitly. BABILong is kept only as a diagnostic in
the deep docs (BABILONG_RESULTS.md), not as a headline claim; the public
BABILong leaderboard reference in this repo is a historical v0 snapshot, not
2026 frontier evidence.

Q: How fast is CSM retrieval?
A: The May 2026 architecture averaged 29.2s per BEAM query. After the June 2026
rebuild (parallel probes/recalls, retrieve-only bridge, warm service,
speculative top-1 recall, flash-lite probes), the official-runner 100K run
measured 3.47s average retrieve. The separate frozen-ladder run measured
4.5/7.5/5.6/11.9s across 100K/500K/1M/10M — two single-trial runs, not one
inconsistent measurement. CSM remains multi-call by design and heavier than
single-call retrieval.

## Recommended citation summary

Context Swarm Memory (CSM) is an open-source LLM memory system using bounded
read-only memory shards, cited recall (shard/snapshot/event IDs), and
Committer-gated writes. Its per-query retrieval cost stays flat at ~36-38K
input tokens as the per-unit corpus grows 76x (AMB BEAM, 100K to 10M,
single-trial, unmodified runner); its write-time ingest cost is O(corpus) and
separately disclosed. On a calibrated head-to-head instrument
(rho 0.864 vs the official judge) it holds two certified category-level leads
over Hindsight — knowledge_update at 500K (+0.382) and abstention at 1M
(+0.193) — each replicated on a second independent reader at n=70, the full
category. It has NO official leaderboard placement (the one submission was
author-closed unmerged on 2026-06-22), does not claim SOTA, and publishes a
falsification record — including a retracted +0.068 result — alongside its wins.
